line_count_note: coverage.json inventoried this image at 31 lines `to the nearest line`. Read line by line it carries 32: the run of entries below the family total of 11 on line 26 is three separate strokes at y≈2633, 2680 and 2713 in the TOTAL column, and the manufactures and commerce columns both carry an entry on the line at y≈2720, which anchors it as its own line rather than part of the one above. The inventory count is superseded by this reading.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.
geometry_note: the leaf is skewed on the exposure: the printed vertical rules drift about 20 px to the left between y=750 and y=2850, measured as a rule-continuity profile in five bands down the page. Every column band used in this reading is sheared by that slope (-0.0095 px per px of y) before its ink is taken, which is why the industry columns separate cleanly at the foot of the sheet as well as at the head.
tool_note: tools/read_census_continuation.py, written for this run of sheets, does not run on this image: it exits `too few vertical rules to name the middle columns`, and on 33S7-9YYJ-9WS, -B1, -B2 and -BF it exits `no industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS`. The skew above is why — its rule finder wants a rule continuous down a fixed x. The reading here was made at magnification against a measured, sheared column map instead. The tool is not weakened to fit; the failure is recorded so the next run does not rediscover it.
right_edge_note: The form's last column — white persons over 20 years of age who cannot read and write — stands at the very edge of the exposure on this image, where the leaf curves into the gutter and the facing page shows through. Nothing is written in it on any line that can be seen, but it is not recorded as empty in either direction: the sheet does not say so.
closure_note: The enumerator added his own totals at the foot of the sheet. Those printed totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and every committed column is checked against them in `column_closure`. A column that does not close keeps its residual and its reading is NOT adjusted to make the total come out — the residual is the finding.

footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: the slaves, pensioners, deaf/dumb/blind/insane and schools blocks carry no figure at the foot of this sheet, and no entry on any of its 32 lines

closes_note: Six of the seven industry columns close exactly, and the seventh and the whole of the rest of the form is blank on the sheet and blank at its foot. Commerce reads 6 against a printed 6; manufactures and trades reads 17 against a printed 17; the learned professions read 5 against a printed 5; mining, agriculture and both navigation columns are empty on every line and carry no footer figure. THE FAMILY TOTALS DO NOT CLOSE, AND THEY DID NOT CLOSE UNDER THE READING THIS ONE REPLACES EITHER: T-0643 read the six matched pairs on lines 1, 5, 13, 19, 24 and 26 as 11 and got 121 against a printed 106, +15; T-0652 re-read them as 4 against a labelled exemplar and gets 79 against the same 106, -27. NEITHER CLOSES, AND NO READING OF THOSE SIX CAN: the other twenty-six lines sum to 55, so the six would have to carry 51, and 4a + 11(6-a) = 51 has no integer solution. The residual is therefore not the six lines' to spend under any assignment, which is why the choice between 4 and 11 was made on the ink and not on the arithmetic. The -27 is left standing and localised in digit_key_used.

pairing.result: THIS IS THE POSITIVE RESULT OF THE TEST. 33S7-9YYJ-8D carries 32 entries, read line by line by T-0643 and anchored by a thirty-second line the inventory had missed. No left sheet in images 1-25 carries 32 entries - eleven of the twelve are ruled to 31 and the twelfth to 30 - so this sheet's left half is NOT in this image group at all. That is a fact about the deposit rather than a failure of the reading, and it is what the other unpaired sheets below should be read against.

digit_key_used.from: 33S7-9YYJ-6Q.json § total_column.digit_key, itself taken from 33S7-9YYJ-24, whose TOTAL column closes at its printed 201 over 31 lines
digit_key_used.ticket: T-0652, which exists because T-0645 settled the same glyph on 33S7-9YYJ-6H and the finding was not to be generalised to this sheet without a reading of this sheet
digit_key_used.what_was_read: the six matched pairs on lines 1, 5, 13, 19, 24 and 26, at 8x-10x, against this leaf’s own confirmed digits and against the arithmetically labelled forms on 33S7-9YYJ-24

why_the_earlier_stroke_pitch_argument_do.what_it_said: T-0643 read the six as 11 because the two strokes stand about 30 px apart, which it measured as the same digit pitch as this sheet’s own footer figures — the two-digit 17 at 32 px and the three-digit 106 at 36 px.
why_the_earlier_stroke_pitch_argument_do.the_metric: left edge to left edge. Under that metric the six measure 26, 28, 23, 33 and 25 px (line 26’s strokes overlap in x and it does not apply), which reproduces the ‘about 30’.
why_the_earlier_stroke_pitch_argument_do.why_it_fails: IT IS NOT A DISCRIMINATOR, and 33S7-9YYJ-24 is where that can be seen, because on that sheet arithmetic labels both classes. Its three committed 4s measure 21, 18 and 39 px left-edge to left-edge, and the gap between the 1 and the 4 of its committed 14 measures 32 px. The gap that separates two DIGITS therefore falls inside the range a single 4 spans, so the measurement cannot tell one from the other on the one sheet where the answer is known. A test that fails on the labelled sheet cannot settle the unlabelled one.
why_the_earlier_stroke_pitch_argument_do.and_the_footer_is_the_wrong_ruler: separately: the footer figures are written larger than the body hand — digit heights 50-56 px against a body stroke mean of 38.7 px — and their own inter-digit gaps, measured axis to axis, are 58.0 px (the 0 and 6 of 106) and 56.6 px (the 1 and 7 of 17), not 36 and 32. Body glyph spacing calibrated on that row is calibrated on a different scale of writing.

digit_key_used.the_metric_used_here: the horizontal distance between the two strokes’ AXES, taken row by row over the rows the two strokes share and averaged. A bounding box widens with the length of a slanted stroke, so box centres and box edges both confound separation with length; the axis distance does not. It is computed from read_census_continuation.py’s own ink mask and components, on the leaf sheared by the -0.0095 px/px already recorded in geometry_note.

what_the_metric_does_on_the_labelled_she.sheet: 33S7-9YYJ-24, TOTAL column, closes at its printed 201
what_the_metric_does_on_the_labelled_she.so: on the sheet where arithmetic labels every glyph, a within-4 separation is 8.3-18.5 px and a between-digit separation is 28.8 px. THIS metric separates the two classes; the left-edge metric does not.

digit_key_used.putting_the_two_sheets_on_one_scale: this leaf’s hand is larger. Over the single-stroke figures of each TOTAL column the mean stroke height is 38.7 px here (n=31, sd 5.6) against 34.9 px on 24 (n=34, sd 5.3), a factor of 1.11. Carried across, 24’s labelled bands become 9.2-20.5 px for a within-4 separation and 31.9 px for a gap between digits, in this sheet’s units.

line 26.note: the two strokes touch; measured without the morphological close

the_six_measured.result: every one of the six lies between 10.1 and 21.3 px. The within-4 band in this sheet’s units is 9.2-20.5 px and a gap between two digits is 31.9 px. Five of the six fall inside the within-4 band outright; line 19 at 21.3 px is 0.8 px above its top and 10.6 px below the bottom of any single labelled 4’s distance from the digit gap. NOT ONE of the six comes within 10 px of a between-digit separation. Read as 11 the sheet would be writing its 11 tighter than the same hand writes the 1 and the 4 of its own 14, which is incoherent.

digit_key_used.the_construction: four of the six — lines 1, 13, 19 and 24 — are the exemplar’s form exactly: a long bold stroke with a shorter companion set below and right. TWO ARE NOT, and are recorded as the weaker readings of the six rather than swept in with the rest. Line 5 is two strokes of equal length standing at the same height, which is the form a reader calls 11 on sight; it is committed 4 on the separation alone, since two digits in this hand do not stand 18.6 px apart. Line 26’s companion lies below and LEFT, mirrored from the exemplar; it is the tightest pair on the sheet at 12.5 px and is committed 4 on the separation and on the mirror being a change of direction rather than of construction. If either is ever overturned it moves the column by 7, to 86 or 93, and neither closes it.

does_the_key_bind_this_sheet.the_question: T-0652 was written not to assume it. 24 is S. W. Sherman’s; this leaf’s printed heading leaves the district blank and division is null, so the sheet does not say who wrote it.
does_the_key_bind_this_sheet.what_was_measured: the slant of every single-stroke figure in each TOTAL column, fitted as mean ink x against y: 33.8 deg (n=34, sd 7.4) on 24 and 35.3 deg (n=31, sd 7.5) here. The means differ by 1.5 deg against a standard error near 1.3 deg apiece — indistinguishable. Stroke aspect (width/height) is 0.95 there and 1.00 here. Scale differs: 34.9 px against 38.7 px of stroke height, about 11 percent, on exposures of near-identical size (4104x3192 and 4056x3208), so it is the pen and not the scan.
does_the_key_bind_this_sheet.the_answer: SUPPORTED, NOT PROVED, and the reading does not rest on it. Slant and aspect are indistinguishable and the scale difference is measured and divided out. More to the point, the argument above is not ‘this is Sherman, so the key applies’: it is that the metric which separates the two classes on a sheet that closes puts all six of this sheet’s figures in one class and none of them near the other, in units of this sheet’s own hand.

where_the_residual_is_and_is_not.not_on_the_six: proved, not asserted: the other twenty-six lines sum to 55, so the six would have to carry 51, and 4a + 11(6-a) = 51 has no integer solution for 0 <= a <= 6. No assignment of 4s and 11s across those six reaches the printed footing. This sheet therefore never offered the closing coincidence 33S7-9YYJ-6Q had to decline.
where_the_residual_is_and_is_not.not_a_lost_companion_stroke_on_the_1s: fourteen lines carry a single bold slash read 1, and a family of one is the obvious place for an unread second stroke. Every line’s TOTAL cell was re-swept at an ink threshold 45 percent lower than the reading’s, with the minimum component area and height dropped with it. Exactly one of the fourteen returns a second shape — line 4 — and at 10x it is one dry-pen stroke broken in the middle, both pieces on a single axis, not a pair. Line 4 stands at 1. Nine of the fourteen would have had to be pairs to carry the -27.
where_the_residual_is_and_is_not.what_is_left: the enumerator’s own addition, or families entered on the left sheet and totalled here in ink this column does not hold. The second cannot be tested from the deposit: T-0642 showed this sheet’s left half is not in images 1-25, since it carries 32 entries and no left sheet in that group carries more than 31. The residual is published and left open, not spread across the lines.
where_the_residual_is_and_is_not.nothing_was_moved_to_close_it: no line reading was adjusted to make the column come out, and the reading reached is the one further from the printed footing than the reading it replaces.
